current_reality.title: Capability and coercive selection
current_reality.summary: Capability advantages under competition create pressure to adopt and reorganise; where concentration pays, power and dependence concentrate, and incumbents keep them.

current_reality.title: Identification and institutional reproduction
current_reality.summary: A proposed spiritual root and the institutions people grow up in reinforce the motives and assumptions that make the present order seem inevitable.

current_reality.title: The paradox of success
current_reality.summary: Alternatives that grow meet demands that shift authority to management; members become customers, and the drift comes to seem realistic.

current_reality.title: Material disruption and security escalation
current_reality.summary: Material limits and growth incentives strain the ecology; scarcity sharpens competition, and threats and countermeasures feed each other.

current_reality.title: AI inside the existing incentive system
current_reality.summary: Deployed by institutions that optimise for accumulation and control, AI can manipulate trust, expand extraction and compound catastrophic risk.

current_reality.title: Why these effects matter for the goal
current_reality.summary: Each problem can independently keep ethical insight from becoming a durable basis for collective life.

conflict.title: Institutional strength and democratic integrity
conflict.summary: A cooperative needs enough capacity to survive, but concentrating authority to get it erodes the member control that made it worth building.

conflict.title: AI capability and resilient autonomy
conflict.summary: A community may need AI to keep up with rivals who use it, yet its essential functions must keep working when AI, power or a provider fails.

conflict.title: Unilateral protection and common security
conflict.summary: Deterrence seems to demand more of a contested capability, while shared survival demands reciprocal limits on that same capability.

conflict.title: Present provision and ecological viability
conflict.summary: Essential services seem to depend on growing material throughput, while ecological limits require constraining it.

conflict.title: Controlled engagement and trustworthy relationships
conflict.summary: A service needs funding to last, but engineering people’s attachment to secure it undermines the free choice that trust depends on.

conflict.title: Success between institutions and integrity within
conflict.summary: Surviving and gaining influence means building what the existing order rewards, but letting its pressures shape the institution erodes the values and relationships it exists for. Leif’s countercurrent’s paradox of success; it may lie behind four of the other five.

future_reality.title: From reflection to democratic coordination
future_reality.summary: Critical inquiry and accessible conflict guidance, under trustworthy governance, build independent competence and lower the cost of conflict, so less authority has to move upward.

future_reality.title: Trust, useful capacity and institutional selection
future_reality.summary: Effective cooperation, trustworthy conduct and controllable capability let an institution keep its mission, be enacted elsewhere and be freely chosen.

future_reality.title: Energy and material capability
future_reality.summary: AI-assisted research helps only if results survive physical tests and deployment; planned simplification is the alternative route, and rebound and delay are the risks.

future_reality.title: Optional model adaptation and field learning
future_reality.summary: Adapting models and bringing an AI voice into real discussions are optional branches with their own tests, and their own risk of a new orthodoxy.

future_reality.title: Common security requires implementation
future_reality.summary: A better discussion cannot by itself change weapons or state behaviour; empowered actors must implement and verify reciprocal limits.

future_reality.title: Risks around inquiry and conflict guidance
future_reality.summary: Each risk is paired with the remedy that must work in practice before relying on the change.

future_reality.title: Risks of dependency, capture and cost
future_reality.summary: Local capability can hide dependency, crowd out essentials, empower new gatekeepers or arrive too early or without governance.

future_reality.title: Risks of growth and replication
future_reality.summary: Copying without people fails, and growth can repeat the old pattern of assimilation.

future_reality.title: Alternative and contested proposals
future_reality.summary: Proposals in the thread that are not agreed changes: some are alternative routes, one is a precaution and one is a contested precondition.

future_reality.title: How the changes reach the goal
future_reality.summary: Four lines of change must hold together, at the relevant scale, for the goal to be reached; global sufficiency is not established.

prerequisite.title: Local capability and practical autonomy

prerequisite.title: Federation with member control

prerequisite.title: Security proposals and actual institutional effects
prerequisite.summary: Dialogue quality and security outcomes are separate endpoints; only empowered actors can implement reciprocal limits.

overview.title: What has to be true
overview.text: The analysis names six success factors for the goal: a liveable future, reflective agency, useful capabilities, trustworthy institutions, keeping the mission while spreading, and learning without a metaphysical test. These are candidate starting points for review.
link: The goal and its six success factors →

overview.title: From a problem to a first action
overview.text: Each row is a published connection, or a reference from one question to another: a problem, the conflict behind it, a change meant to address both, the effects it should have on the way to the goal, and the step and action that would put it into practice.

overview.title: Where needs pull two ways
overview.text: The analysis finds five conflicts in the discussion, and Leif’s countercurrent’s paradox of success adds a sixth that may lie behind four of them. The first sits behind the problem of central intervention: a cooperative needs enough capacity to survive, but concentrating authority to get it erodes the member control that made it worth building.

overview.title: Try conflict guidance that members can question and leave
overview.text: The proposal is to test useful guidance while members retain control, access to human help and competence without the tool. It is one candidate way through the first conflict: if members can work through disagreements themselves, less authority needs to move upward. Each of the analysis’s fifteen risks comes with a remedy like the one beside it.
link: The changes, their effects and their risks →

overview.title: What would change our minds?
overview.text: Do destructive conflict costs and unnecessary escalation fall, while fair treatment, independent competence and member influence remain? Fewer complaints or higher satisfaction would not settle it: costs may have moved elsewhere, or justified grievances may have been suppressed. A local success would still leave open whether small democratic groups gain enough to change which institutions survive.
link: Inspect the test and what remains open →

overview.title: Choose one willing host and one function
overview.text: No trial is recorded here. The first task is to establish a bounded case and check what already operates; measures, protections, responsibilities and resources follow, agreed with the people affected. A missing detail in an analysis does not prove that a host lacks it.

overview.title: One entry point into a broader programme
overview.text: The map also covers reflective development, trustworthy governance, model adaptation, voice participation, federation, material and energy services, and common security, each with its own risks, first steps and tests. Conflict guidance is one possible starting point; no single global constraint has been established.

backlog.label: Compare AI guidance with optional-AI and human approaches.
backlog.note: Check useful output, total cost, energy, member control, fallback and competence without the tool. Participants have not committed to running this comparison.

backlog.label: Decide in advance what evidence would change the hypothesis.
backlog.note: Lower satisfaction scores or fewer complaints alone do not establish benefit. The first analysis asks whether small democratic groups gain more than hierarchies; the second distinguishes local improvements from the still-unclosed institutional-selection claim F17. One successful pilot cannot establish the larger claim.

backlog.label: Assess suppressed grievances separately from satisfaction.
backlog.note: Retain independent human support and a way to report costs, unfairness, dependency and increased concentration of authority.

backlog.label: Test 1: does reflection become transferable judgment, not just agreeable dialogue?
backlog.note: Prediction: against a suitable comparison, participants identify and revise consequential assumptions, consider contrary perspectives and act differently on later tasks. Defeated if benefits vanish outside the dialogue, depend on agreeing with the facilitator, or weaken independent judgment. Protect voluntary participation, correction and human support; no ontology score as the outcome.

backlog.label: Test 2: does conflict guidance reduce destructive costs and the pressure to centralise?
backlog.note: Prediction: over a defined period and comparison, destructive conflict costs and unnecessary hierarchical intervention fall while fair treatment, independent competence and member influence hold or improve. Defeated if only satisfaction or complaint counts improve, costs move elsewhere, structural grievances are hidden or authority concentrates. Protect confidentiality, voluntariness and independent human help, and measure justice, capability and control separately.

backlog.label: Test 3: does community-controlled AI give useful capability with practical autonomy?
backlog.note: Prediction: the same useful service meets agreed quality and whole-cost limits, and migration or disruption tests show acceptable continuity without depending on a provider’s discretion. Defeated if quality or cost is unacceptable, one specialist stays indispensable, or exit and continuity fail in practice. Stage investment, keep the baseline service and test a feasible fallback.

backlog.label: Test 4: does the Forge produce stable benefits and its claimed resource advantage?
backlog.note: Prediction: a reproducible adaptation beats controls on held-out useful tasks and critical reflection without relevant regressions, and any energy claim is measured for comparable output. Defeated if only philosophical self-reports change, gains reflect selected prompts, other capabilities regress or resource costs do not improve. Keep functional performance, consciousness claims, model preferences and energy separate, and retain rollback.

backlog.label: Test 5: does federation supply coordination without a new centre of domination?
backlog.note: Prediction: the joint service improves coordination at acceptable cost while decision rights, exit and continuity survive disputed decisions and the loss of a participant. Defeated if coordination costs exceed gains, a gatekeeper gains unilateral control, or nominal decentralisation hides dependence. Keep authority traceable, updates bounded and reversible, exit meaningful and evaluation independent.

backlog.label: Test 6: do AI-assisted innovation and distributed provision improve services within limits?
backlog.note: Prediction: a physically verified, deployed option meets the service requirements, whole costs, ownership conditions and total ecological limits within the transition window. Defeated if results stay at prediction or laboratory stage, essential inputs are unavailable, deployment comes too late, or total demand offsets efficiency. Keep readiness stages separate and preserve essential provision if the transition is delayed or fails.

backlog.label: Test 7: do constructive practices reproduce and keep their mission under growth?
backlog.note: Prediction: independent sites enact the practice and keep useful performance, justified trust and member control through an agreed period and changes in scale. Defeated if originators stay essential, adoption is symbolic, costs are hidden, or market success comes with democratic erosion. Measure selection within institutions separately from survival and adoption between them.

backlog.label: Test 8: can security inquiry contribute to less escalatory institutions?
backlog.note: Prediction: a proposal survives critical review, is implemented by empowered actors and produces observable reciprocal compliance and less escalatory conduct without sacrificing protected rights. Defeated if only the discussion improves, powerful actors ignore the rules, or a coalition increases threats and armament. Require verification, accountability, rights protection and explicit review of escalatory effects.

backlog.label: Test 9: do voice participation and the field-learning loop improve real deliberation?
backlog.note: Prediction: against a conversational baseline, the group handles important assumptions and decisions better without reduced participation or unapproved collection, and approved learning material leads to a separately tested improvement. Defeated if latency or interruption reduces participation, the AI becomes an authority, or no benefit outlasts conversational appeal. Keep human interruption and correction, voluntary participation, confidentiality and separate permission for any training use.

backlog.label: Test 10: does justified trust become a practical institutional advantage?
backlog.note: Prediction: where people have feasible alternatives and comparable service, trustworthy conduct supports voluntary participation, sustained cooperation and useful contributions while member agency stays intact. Defeated if reported confidence rises without warranted conduct, people cannot really choose, or resources and authority concentrate despite adoption. Record conduct, confidence, freedom to choose, cooperation and decision rights separately, and do not infer justice from market success.

backlog.label: Is changing which institutions get selected the deepest leverage available?
backlog.note: Show whether a capability, governance or material change improves durable humane outcomes more than a human-development, institutional or non-AI comparator. Leif argues AI may be the deepest leverage point; Robert locates it in the power to transcend paradigms, and Leif has asked him to confirm or correct that reading.

backlog.label: Is engagement with AI necessary for lasting emancipation?
backlog.note: Identify the particular function and competitive threat, and compare adequate non-AI and optional-AI arrangements. Historical recurrence alone does not establish future necessity.

backlog.label: Does philosophical coherence give a computational or energy advantage?
backlog.note: This needs matched useful-task and resource measurements on reproducible variants, with performance, inference effort, hardware and total costs kept distinct.

backlog.label: Does a distributed architecture resist all three structural fates?
backlog.note: Exercise actual dependencies, control rights, update integrity, loss of participants and credible capture routes; replace claims of immunity with bounded, demonstrated resilience.

backlog.label: Can AI research change the energy transition in time?
backlog.note: Track readiness and deployment at service scale, with financing, manufacturing, materials, ownership and continuing provision.

backlog.label: Does reflective or spiritual maturity cause enduring institutional change?

current_reality.title: Capability and coercive selection
current_reality.summary: Capability advantages under competition create pressure to adopt and reorganise; where concentration pays, power and dependence concentrate, and incumbents keep them.

current_reality.title: Identification and institutional reproduction
current_reality.summary: A proposed spiritual root and the institutions people grow up in reinforce the motives and assumptions that make the present order seem inevitable.

current_reality.title: The paradox of success
current_reality.summary: Alternatives that grow meet demands that shift authority to management; members become customers, and the drift comes to seem realistic.

current_reality.title: Material disruption and security escalation
current_reality.summary: Material limits and growth incentives strain the ecology; scarcity sharpens competition, and threats and countermeasures feed each other.

current_reality.title: AI inside the existing incentive system
current_reality.summary: Deployed by institutions that optimise for accumulation and control, AI can manipulate trust, expand extraction and compound catastrophic risk.

current_reality.title: Why these effects matter for the goal
current_reality.summary: Each problem can independently keep ethical insight from becoming a durable basis for collective life.

conflict.title: Institutional strength and democratic integrity
conflict.summary: A cooperative needs enough capacity to survive, but concentrating authority to get it erodes the member control that made it worth building.

conflict.title: AI capability and resilient autonomy
conflict.summary: A community may need AI to keep up with rivals who use it, yet its essential functions must keep working when AI, power or a provider fails.

conflict.title: Unilateral protection and common security
conflict.summary: Deterrence seems to demand more of a contested capability, while shared survival demands reciprocal limits on that same capability.

conflict.title: Present provision and ecological viability
conflict.summary: Essential services seem to depend on growing material throughput, while ecological limits require constraining it.

conflict.title: Controlled engagement and trustworthy relationships
conflict.summary: A service needs funding to last, but engineering people’s attachment to secure it undermines the free choice that trust depends on.

conflict.title: Success between institutions and integrity within
conflict.summary: Surviving and gaining influence means building what the existing order rewards, but letting its pressures shape the institution erodes the values and relationships it exists for. Leif’s countercurrent’s paradox of success; it may lie behind four of the other five.

future_reality.title: From reflection to democratic coordination
future_reality.summary: Critical inquiry and accessible conflict guidance, under trustworthy governance, build independent competence and lower the cost of conflict, so less authority has to move upward.

future_reality.title: Trust, useful capacity and institutional selection
future_reality.summary: Effective cooperation, trustworthy conduct and controllable capability let an institution keep its mission, be enacted elsewhere and be freely chosen.

future_reality.title: Energy and material capability
future_reality.summary: AI-assisted research helps only if results survive physical tests and deployment; planned simplification is the alternative route, and rebound and delay are the risks.

future_reality.title: Optional model adaptation and field learning
future_reality.summary: Adapting models and bringing an AI voice into real discussions are optional branches with their own tests, and their own risk of a new orthodoxy.

future_reality.title: Common security requires implementation
future_reality.summary: A better discussion cannot by itself change weapons or state behaviour; empowered actors must implement and verify reciprocal limits.

future_reality.title: Risks around inquiry and conflict guidance
future_reality.summary: Each risk is paired with the remedy that must work in practice before relying on the change.

future_reality.title: Risks of dependency, capture and cost
future_reality.summary: Local capability can hide dependency, crowd out essentials, empower new gatekeepers or arrive too early or without governance.

future_reality.title: Risks of growth and replication
future_reality.summary: Copying without people fails, and growth can repeat the old pattern of assimilation.

future_reality.title: Alternative and contested proposals

future_reality.summary: Four lines of change must hold together, at the relevant scale, for the goal to be reached; global sufficiency is not established.

prerequisite.title: Shared foundations
prerequisite.summary: Choose the case first; then inventory assets, agree measures, settle rights and commit resources, which can proceed in parallel.

prerequisite.title: Field practice and continuing operation
prerequisite.summary: Whichever practice is chosen must be ready and authorised before a bounded comparison; only a review that could reject it supports continuing.

prerequisite.title: Local capability and practical autonomy
prerequisite.summary: Autonomy means a useful service at whole cost with tested fallback, not owning hardware.

prerequisite.title: Model adaptation and voice learning
prerequisite.summary: Adapting a model and adding an AI voice have separate prerequisites; neither is required for the other.

prerequisite.title: Federation with member control
prerequisite.summary: A network that runs is not yet a network that adds value or disperses power.

prerequisite.title: Useful energy and material services
prerequisite.summary: Physical evidence, then production and ownership, then a reliable service within limits; a mature existing option can satisfy the first step.

prerequisite.title: Independent replication without mission loss
prerequisite.summary: Another community needs more than a document: people, resources, governance and an honest account of failures.

prerequisite.title: Security proposals and actual institutional effects
prerequisite.summary: Dialogue quality and security outcomes are separate endpoints; only empowered actors can implement reciprocal limits.

overview.title: What has to be true
overview.text: The analysis names six success factors for the goal: a liveable future, reflective agency, useful capabilities, trustworthy institutions, keeping the mission while spreading, and learning without a metaphysical test. These are candidate starting points for review.
link: The goal and its six success factors →

overview.title: From a problem to a first action
overview.text: Each row is a published connection, or a reference from one question to another: a problem, the conflict behind it, a change meant to address both, the effects it should have on the way to the goal, and the step and action that would put it into practice.

overview.title: Where needs pull two ways
overview.text: The analysis finds five conflicts in the discussion, and Leif’s countercurrent’s paradox of success adds a sixth that may lie behind four of them. The first sits behind the problem of central intervention: a cooperative needs enough capacity to survive, but concentrating authority to get it erodes the member control that made it worth building.

overview.title: Try conflict guidance that members can question and leave
overview.text: The proposal is to test useful guidance while members retain control, access to human help and competence without the tool. It is one candidate way through the first conflict: if members can work through disagreements themselves, less authority needs to move upward. Each of the analysis’s fifteen risks comes with a remedy like the one beside it.
link: The changes, their effects and their risks →

overview.title: What would change our minds?
overview.text: Do destructive conflict costs and unnecessary escalation fall, while fair treatment, independent competence and member influence remain? Fewer complaints or higher satisfaction would not settle it: costs may have moved elsewhere, or justified grievances may have been suppressed. A local success would still leave open whether small democratic groups gain enough to change which institutions survive.

overview.title: Choose one willing host and one function
overview.text: No trial is recorded here. The first task is to establish a bounded case and check what already operates; measures, protections, responsibilities and resources follow, agreed with the people affected. A missing detail in an analysis does not prove that a host lacks it.

overview.title: One entry point into a broader programme
overview.text: The map also covers reflective development, trustworthy governance, model adaptation, voice participation, federation, material and energy services, and common security, each with its own risks, first steps and tests. Conflict guidance is one possible starting point; no single global constraint has been established.
